description: ANA* (Anytime Nonparametric A*) finds a first path fast and then improves it, with no weight schedule to tune. With `G` the cost of the best solution so far, it expands the open state with the largest `e = (G − g) / h`: the state that could reach a goal with the most slack below `G`. It drops every state with `g + h ≥ G`, so each new goal it finds is cheaper than the one before. Before the first solution it orders by `h` alone, like greedy best-first search. With an *admissible* `h` (it never overestimates), the last solution is optimal, and each report comes with a lower bound on the optimal cost.

papers.authors: Jur van den Berg, Rajat Shah, Arthur Huang, Ken Goldberg
